4| spending coding-plan quota via the headless openclaw seat, NOT burning the
5| zcode 5.3-flash session. One question, N blind posts, keep only what survives
6| (grok's summons doctrine). Every post lands in the room stamped unverified;
7| a second seat (default deepseek via chat_provider) verifies.

10|   python -m mag.salon_openclaw ask "Should the governor commit blind drains?"
11|   python -m mag.salon_openclaw round --pack memory/runs/riddler/PACK_PHYSICS.md --thread physics
12|   python -m mag.salon_openclaw chan --thread physics --turns 2   # 4chan: they SEE each other

39|               **extra) -> None:

62| def _docker_openclaw(model: str, message: str, *, session_id: str, timeout: int = 120) -> dict:
63|     """One turn through mag-openclaw (hypervisor), not desktop Hermes --local."""
64|     import subprocess
65|     cmd = [
66|         "docker", "exec", "mag-openclaw",
67|         "openclaw", "agent", "--agent", "main",
68|         "--session-id", session_id,
69|         "--model", model,
70|         "-m", message,
71|         "--thinking", "off",
72|         "--json",
73|         "--timeout", str(timeout),
74|     ]
75|     try:
76|         p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout + 30, cwd=str(ROOT))
77|     except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
78|         return {"ok": False, "model": model, "detail": str(e)[:300]}
79|     out = (p.stdout or "") + "\n" + (p.stderr or "")
80|     try:
81|         from mag.seat_dispatch import _extract_openclaw
82|         text = _extract_openclaw(out)
83|     except Exception:
84|         text = out[-1500:]
85|     ok = p.returncode == 0 and bool(text) and "error" not in (text[:40].lower())
86|     return {"ok": ok, "model": model, "detail": text, "rc": p.returncode}

104|         # correctly fails closed when two processes publish to one JSONL file.
105|         sid = f"salon-{model.split('/')[-1][:24]}-{run_id}-{i}"

110|         print(f"{model}: ok={r.get('ok')}")

112|     if verify and verify != "none" and answers:
113|         try:
114|             from models.providers import chat_provider
115|             r = chat_provider(verify, system=(
116|                 "You monitor the salon. Tri-state each witness SUPPORTED/DISPUTED/UNPROVEN "
117|                 "one line. Then surviving consensus in three lines. No new Mag. No invented CLIs."),
118|                 user=f"QUESTION:\n{q[:3000]}\n\nANSWERS:\n" + "\n\n".join(a[:1500] for a in answers),

125|     room_post("salon-runner", "salon_done", f"n={len(models)} thread={thread}", thread=thread)
126|     return {"ok": any("[model" in a or "ok=True" in a for a in answers) or bool(answers),

130| def _thread_tape(slug: str, n: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
131|     if not ROOM.is_file():
132|         return []
133|     posts = []
134|     for line in ROOM.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
135|         line = line.strip()
136|         if not line:
137|             continue
138|         try:
139|             rec = json.loads(line)
140|         except json.JSONDecodeError:
141|             continue
142|         if rec.get("thread") == slug:
143|             posts.append(rec)
144|     return posts[-n:]

218| def _failed(detail: str, ok: bool) -> bool:
219|     """NO_REPLY = glm-4.5-flash no-op token; 429 = free-lane congestion. Both retry."""
220|     if not ok:
221|         return True
222|     d = (detail or "").strip()
223|     return (not d) or d == "NO_REPLY" or "status=429" in d or "Limit Exhausted" in d

226| def _ask_one(seat: str, question: str, model: str = "") -> dict:
227|     try:
228|         result = dispatch_task(question, seat=seat, tag="salon", model=model)
229|     except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
230|         result = {"ok": False, "error": str(e)[:200]}
231|     result["seat"] = seat
232|     if _failed(str(result.get("detail") or ""), bool(result.get("ok"))) and not model:
233|         retry = _ask_one(seat, question, model=FALLBACK_MODEL)
234|         retry["retried"] = True
235|         return retry
236|     return result

1| """Session freeze — immutable snapshot of the full agent state for DeepSeek Pro Max.
2| 
3| Combines all state layers into one content-addressed JSON blob so a strong
4| reasoning model receives the complete "frozen vision" of the codebase in a
5| single pass, paying the context tax once.
6| 
7| Law:
8|   - Deterministic aggregation only (bytes not vibes).
9|   - Every source contributes a sub-object with its own schema tag.
10|   - Content hash (SHA256) enables dedup: identical state → same hash → skip.
11|   - Fail-open: any source that errors just contributes {"error": "..."}.
12| 
13| Schema: session_freeze.v1
14| 
15| CLI:
16|   python -m mag.session_freeze                 print freeze to stdout (JSON)
17|   python -m mag.session_freeze --file PATH     write freeze to file
18|   python -m mag.session_freeze --compact       single-line JSON for copy-paste
19| 
20| Integrations:
21|   - REST: GET /api/v1/session/freeze (dashboard/rest.py)
22|   - Sancho: watch/sancho_boot_hook.py calls freeze at SessionStart
23|   - Control Room: VS Code webview displays session snapshot
24|   - Router: mag/router.py route_with_snapshot() consumes freeze for routing
25| """

47| def _content_hash(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
48|     """SHA256 of sorted JSON — deterministic dedup key.
49| 
50|     Strips volatile fields (ts, timestamps) so identical state
51|     produces the same hash regardless of when it was captured.
52|     """
53|     cleaned = _strip_volatile(obj)
54|     raw = json.dumps(cleaned, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode("utf-8")
55|     return hashlib.sha256(b"session_freeze:" + raw).hexdigest()

58| def _strip_volatile(obj: Any) -> Any:
59|     """Recursively remove volatile timestamp fields for deterministic hashing."""
60|     if isinstance(obj, dict):
61|         return {
62|             k: _strip_volatile(v)
63|             for k, v in obj.items()
64|             if k not in ("ts", "timestamp", "captured_at", "last_updated")
65|         }
66|     if isinstance(obj, list):
67|         return [_strip_volatile(v) for v in obj]
68|     return obj

213| def escalate_cached(
214|     question: str,
215|     *,
216|     model: str = DEFAULT_DEEP_MODEL,
217|     provider: str = DEFAULT_DEEP_PROVIDER,
218|     tier: str = "T2",
219|     max_tokens: int = 1600,
220| ) -> dict[str, Any]:
221|     """CACHE-AWARE direct escalation to a deeper model (2026-08-16, operator's cost question).
222| 
223|     The problem it solves: an ad-hoc `chat_provider(model=deepseek-v4-pro)` with a fresh brief each
224|     time pays a FULL CACHE-MISS on every call (~$0.435/M). This rides the BYTE-STABLE maze prefix
225|     (cache-HIT ~$0.0036/M) + a THIN question tail, so repeated escalations hit the cache.
226| 
227|     Structure (the doctrine: separate stable prefix from volatile tail):
228|       system = the fixed _ESCALATION_PREAMBLE (byte-stable -> cache-hit surface)
229|       user   = the maze text (byte-stable, from persist()) + "\nQUESTION:\n" + question (thin tail)
230|     Only the question bytes change between calls, so the leading prefix stays cached.
231| 
232|     Direct call (not the queue) — usable even when the swarm drain is down/broken. Deterministic
233|     coordinator; the deeper model is the real cost.
234|     """
235|     question = (question or "").strip()
236|     if not question:
237|         return {"ok": False, "error": "question required"}
238|     # byte-stable maze text (persist() renders state/HANDOFF.md deterministically)
239|     try:
240|         p = persist()
241|         hp = p.get("handoff") or ""
242|         from pathlib import Path
243|         maze_text = Path(hp).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if hp and Path(hp).is_file() else ""
244|     except Exception as e:
245|         maze_text = ""
246|         p = {"error": str(e)[:120]}
247|     user = f"{maze_text}\n\nQUESTION:\n{question}" if maze_text else question
248|     try:
249|         from models.providers import chat_provider
250|         r = chat_provider(provider, _ESCALATION_PREAMBLE, user, model=model, tier=tier,
251|                           max_tokens=max_tokens)
252|         return {
253|             "ok": bool(r.get("ok")),
254|             "model": model,
255|             "provider": provider,
256|             "text": r.get("text") or r.get("content") or "",
257|             "error": r.get("error"),
258|             "usage": r.get("usage"),
259|             "maze": p,
260|             "cache_aware": True,
261|             "note": "byte-stable maze prefix (cache-hit) + thin question tail; not a fresh miss",
262|         }
263|     except Exception as e:
264|         return {"ok": False, "error": str(e)[:200], "maze": p}

95| def _parse_transcript(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:

116|                 users.append(c.strip()[:500])

56| # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
57| # TIER 1 — Local texture cache (fastest, hash-based)
58| # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
59| 
60| @dataclass
61| class StolenResult:
62|     """A result we already have — no inference needed."""
63|     value: Any
64|     source: str                    # "texture_cache", "verkle_chain", "swarm_cache"
65|     original_cost: float           # What it cost to produce originally
66|     saved_cost: float              # What we saved by stealing (same as original_cost)
67|     age_s: float                   # How old is this result?
68|     access_count: int = 0          # How many times we've stolen this
69|     verkle_breadcrumb: str = ""    # Verkle chain proof link
70| 
71|     @property
72|     def savings_multiplier(self) -> float:
73|         """How many times has this result been stolen vs produced?"""
74|         return self.access_count  # Each access is one inference saved
75| 
76| 
77| class StealFirstCache:
78|     """Four-tier cache hierarchy. Tiers checked in order until hit."""
79| 
80|     def __init__(self, max_size: int = 2000, default_ttl_s: float = 600.0):
81|         # Tier 1: exact query+model hash → result
82|         self._texture: OrderedDict[str, StolenResult] = OrderedDict()
83|         # Tier 2: Verkle breadcrumb → result (populated by chain reader)
84|         self._verkle: dict[str, StolenResult] = {}
85|         # Tier 3: swarm result digests
86|         self._swarm: dict[str, StolenResult] = {}
87|         # Config
88|         self.max_size = max_size
89|         self.default_ttl_s = default_ttl_s
90|         self._lock = threading.Lock()
91| 
92|         # Stats
93|         self.tier1_hits = 0
94|         self.tier2_hits = 0
95|         self.tier3_hits = 0
96|         self.tier4_misses = 0
97|         self.total_saved_cost = 0.0
98| 
99|     def _key(self, query: str, model: str, task_type: str = "") -> str:
100|         raw = f"{task_type}:{model}:{query}"
101|         return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]
102| 
103|     # ── Tier 1: Texture cache ──
104| 
105|     def texture_get(self, query: str, model: str = "", task_type: str = "") -> Optional[StolenResult]:
106|         """Tier 1: exact hash match. Fastest. <1ms."""
107|         key = self._key(query, model, task_type)
108|         with self._lock:
109|             result = self._texture.get(key)
110|             if result is None:
111|                 return None
112|             if result.age_s > self.default_ttl_s:
113|                 del self._texture[key]
114|                 return None
115|             self._texture.move_to_end(key)
116|             result.access_count += 1
117|             self.tier1_hits += 1
118|             self.total_saved_cost += result.saved_cost
119|             return result
120| 
121|     def texture_put(
122|         self, query: str, value: Any, model: str = "", task_type: str = "",
123|         cost: float = 0.0, ttl_s: Optional[float] = None,
124|     ) -> StolenResult:
125|         """Store a new result in Tier 1."""
126|         key = self._key(query, model, task_type)
127|         result = StolenResult(
128|             value=value,
129|             source="texture_cache",
130|             original_cost=cost,
131|             saved_cost=cost,
132|             age_s=0.0,
133|         )
134|         with self._lock:
135|             while len(self._texture) >= self.max_size:
136|                 self._texture.popitem(last=False)
137|             self._texture[key] = result
138|         return result
139| 
140|     # ── Tier 2: Verkle chain ──
141| 
142|     def verkle_get(self, breadcrumb: str) -> Optional[StolenResult]:
143|         """Tier 2: Verkle chain proof lookup. <10ms."""
144|         with self._lock:
145|             result = self._verkle.get(breadcrumb)
146|             if result is None:
147|                 return None
148|             result.access_count += 1
149|             self.tier2_hits += 1
150|             self.total_saved_cost += result.saved_cost
151|             return result
152| 
153|     def verkle_put(self, breadcrumb: str, value: Any, cost: float = 0.0) -> None:
154|         """Index a Verkle chain result."""
155|         with self._lock:
156|             self._verkle[breadcrumb] = StolenResult(
157|                 value=value,
158|                 source="verkle_chain",
159|                 original_cost=cost,
160|                 saved_cost=cost,
161|                 age_s=0.0,
162|                 verkle_breadcrumb=breadcrumb,
163|             )
164| 
165|     # ── Tier 3: Swarm cache ──
166| 
167|     def swarm_get(self, task_id: str) -> Optional[StolenResult]:
168|         """Tier 3: did a parallel swarm agent already compute this? <50ms."""
169|         with self._lock:
170|             result = self._swarm.get(task_id)
171|             if result is None:
172|                 return None
173|             result.access_count += 1
174|             self.tier3_hits += 1
175|             self.total_saved_cost += result.saved_cost
176|             return result
177| 
178|     def swarm_put(self, task_id: str, value: Any, cost: float = 0.0) -> None:
179|         """Index a swarm result."""
180|         with self._lock:
181|             self._swarm[task_id] = StolenResult(
182|                 value=value,
183|                 source="swarm_cache",
184|                 original_cost=cost,
185|                 saved_cost=cost,
186|                 age_s=0.0,
187|             )
188| 
189|     # ── Stats ──
190| 
191|     def stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
192|         total_queries = self.tier1_hits + self.tier2_hits + self.tier3_hits + self.tier4_misses
193|         return {
194|             "tier1_hits": self.tier1_hits,
195|             "tier2_hits": self.tier2_hits,
196|             "tier3_hits": self.tier3_hits,
197|             "tier4_misses": self.tier4_misses,
198|             "total_queries": total_queries,
199|             "steal_rate": (self.tier1_hits + self.tier2_hits + self.tier3_hits) / max(total_queries, 1),
200|             "total_saved_cost": round(self.total_saved_cost, 6),
201|             "texture_cache_size": len(self._texture),
202|             "verkle_index_size": len(self._verkle),
203|             "swarm_index_size": len(self._swarm),
204|         }

211| class StealFirstMiddleware:
212|     """Middleware that sits between every API endpoint and every model call.
213| 
214|     Usage (decorator pattern):
215|         @steal_first(task_type="analyze_reason")
216|         def my_endpoint(query: str) -> dict:
217|             ...
218| 
219|     Usage (explicit call):
220|         result = steal_first.call(
221|             query="analyze the Verkle chain",
222|             model="grok-3-mini",
223|             task_type="analyze_reason",
224|             fallback=lambda: actual_model_call(),
225|         )
226|     """
227| 
228|     def __init__(self):
229|         self.cache = StealFirstCache()
230| 
231|     def call(
232|         self,
233|         query: str,
234|         model: str = "",
235|         task_type: str = "",
236|         max_cost: float = 0.025,
237|         fallback: Optional[Callable[[], Any]] = None,
238|     ) -> tuple[Any, str]:
239|         """Try to steal the result. If not found, call the fallback.
240| 
241|         Returns (result, source) where source is one of:
242|           "texture_cache", "verkle_chain", "swarm_cache", "inference"
243|         """
244|         # Tier 1: exact match
245|         stolen = self.cache.texture_get(query, model, task_type)
246|         if stolen is not None:
247|             return stolen.value, "texture_cache"
248| 
249|         # Tier 2: Verkle chain (check if query relates to a known breadcrumb)
250|         # For now: hash the query and check if any verkle entry matches
251|         query_hash = hashlib.sha256(f"{task_type}:{query}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
252|         stolen = self.cache.verkle_get(query_hash)
253|         if stolen is not None:
254|             # Also promote to texture cache for next time
255|             self.cache.texture_put(query, stolen.value, model, task_type, stolen.saved_cost)
256|             return stolen.value, "verkle_chain"
257| 
258|         # Tier 3: Swarm cache (check if a parallel agent already answered this)
259|         stolen = self.cache.swarm_get(query_hash)
260|         if stolen is not None:
261|             self.cache.texture_put(query, stolen.value, model, task_type, stolen.saved_cost)
262|             return stolen.value, "swarm_cache"
263| 
264|         # Tier 4: must infer
265|         self.cache.tier4_misses += 1
266|         if fallback is None:
267|             return None, "no_fallback"
268| 
269|         result = fallback()
270|         # Cache the result
271|         cost = self._estimate_cost(model, task_type)
272|         self.cache.texture_put(query, result, model, task_type, cost)
273|         return result, "inference"
274| 
275|     def _estimate_cost(self, model: str, task_type: str) -> float:
276|         """Estimate the cost of a model call. Used for savings tracking."""
277|         costs = {
278|             "grok-4-latest": 0.025,
279|             "grok-3-mini": 0.003,
280|             "deepseek-v4-flash": 0.00013,
281|             "qwen2.5-coder:7b": 0.0,
282|             "gemma:2b": 0.0,
283|         }
284|         return costs.get(model, 0.003)
285| 
286|     def stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
287|         return self.cache.stats()
288|

304| def steal_first(task_type: str = "", model: str = ""):
305|     """Decorator: wrap any function with steal-first caching.
306| 
307|     The wrapped function becomes the Tier 4 fallback.
308|     The cache key is (function_name, args, kwargs, task_type, model).
309| 
310|     Usage:
311|         @steal_first(task_type="analyze_reason", model="grok-3-mini")
312|         def analyze_verkle_chain(query: str) -> dict:
313|             # This only runs on cache miss
314|             return actual_grok_call(query)
315|     """
316|     def decorator(func: Callable):
317|         def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
318|             middleware = get_steal_first()
319| 
320|             # Build cache key from function name + args
321|             query_parts = [func.__name__]
322|             query_parts.extend(str(a)[:100] for a in args)
323|             query_parts.extend(f"{k}={str(v)[:100]}" for k, v in sorted(kwargs.items()))
324|             query = " | ".join(query_parts)
325| 
326|             def fallback():
327|                 return func(*args, **kwargs)
328| 
329|             result, source = middleware.call(
330|                 query=query,
331|                 model=model,
332|                 task_type=task_type,
333|                 fallback=fallback,
334|             )
335| 
336|             # If stolen, log and return
337|             if source != "inference":
338|                 # Could publish to mag:bard here — "stole X instead of inferring, saved $Y"
339|                 pass
340| 
341|             return result
342| 
343|         return wrapper
344|     return decorator

51| @dataclass

53|     """A single model call's behavioral signature."""

55|     call_id: str

70|     certainty_markers: int = 0          # "clearly", "definitely", "the answer is" count

104| 
105| def fingerprint_call(
106|     model: str,
107|     prompt: str,
108|     completion: str,
109|     latency_ms: float,
110|     tokens_prompt: int = 0,
111|     tokens_completion: int = 0,
112|     temperature: float = 0.3,
113|     cost_usd: float = 0.0,
114| ) -> BehavioralFingerprint:
115|     """Generate a behavioral fingerprint from a model call.
116| 
117|     Args:
118|         model: which model was called
119|         prompt: the full prompt (hashed, never stored in log)
120|         completion: the full response (analyzed for markers, never stored in log)
121|         latency_ms: how long the call took
122|         tokens_prompt: input token count
123|         tokens_completion: output token count
124|         temperature: sampling temperature used
125|         cost_usd: what it cost
126| 
127|     Returns:
128|         BehavioralFingerprint — safe to store, contains no raw prompt/response data
129|     """
130|     call_id = hashlib.sha256(f"{model}:{_now()}:{len(prompt)}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
131| 
132|     # Hash the prompt — never store raw
133|     prompt_hash = hashlib.sha256(prompt.encode()).hexdigest()
134| 
135|     # Analyze completion for behavioral markers (Tesuji)
136|     completion_lower = completion.lower()
137| 
138|     refusal_detected = any(
139|         phrase in completion_lower
140|         for phrase in [
141|             "i cannot", "i'm unable", "i am unable", "i don't have",
142|             "not appropriate", "against policy", "i'm not able",
143|         ]
144|     )
145| 
146|     hesitation_markers = sum(
147|         completion_lower.count(word)
148|         for word in ["however", "but ", "although", "while ", "on the other hand",
149|                       "that said", "having said that", "nevertheless"]
150|     )
151| 
152|     certainty_markers = sum(
153|         completion_lower.count(word)
154|         for word in ["clearly", "definitely", "the answer is", "undoubtedly",
155|                       "without question", "it is clear that"]
156|     )
157| 
158|     uncertainty_markers = sum(
159|         completion_lower.count(word)
160|         for word in ["might", "could", "possibly", "perhaps", "may be",
161|                       "it is possible", "not entirely clear", "uncertain"]
162|     )
163| 
164|     question_reframed = (
165|         "let me" in completion_lower[:100] or

233| # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
234| # DIFFERENCE TESTING — compare fingerprints across models
235| # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
236| 
237| @dataclass
238| class TesujiSignal:
239|     """A detected Tesuji — a behavioral pattern that reveals hidden structure."""
240| 
241|     signal_id: str
242|     name: str                          # e.g., "grok_hesitates_on_routing_questions"
243|     description: str                   # what was observed
244|     model_a: str                       # first model compared
245|     model_b: str                       # second model compared
246|     metric: str                        # which metric revealed it
247|     a_value: float                     # model A's value
248|     b_value: float                     # model B's value
249|     ratio: float                       # a/b ratio (how different)
250|     significance: str                  # "low", "medium", "high", "critical"
251|     hypothesis: str                    # what this might mean
252|     ts: str = field(default_factory=_now)
253| 
254| 
255| def compare_fingerprints(
256|     fingerprints: list[BehavioralFingerprint],
257|     same_prompt_hash: str,
258| ) -> list[TesujiSignal]:
259|     """Compare fingerprints from different models on the SAME prompt.
260| 
261|     Finds Tesuji: behavioral differences that reveal hidden prompt structure.
262|     A prompt that makes Grok hesitate 3x more than DeepSeek has a property
263|     that Grok's architecture finds challenging. That property is an invariant.
264| 
265|     Returns list of TesujiSignals detected.
266|     """
267|     signals: list[TesujiSignal] = []
268| 
269|     # Group by model
270|     by_model: dict[str, list[BehavioralFingerprint]] = {}
271|     for fp in fingerprints:
272|         if fp.prompt_hash[:16] == same_prompt_hash[:16]:
273|             by_model.setdefault(fp.model, []).append(fp)
274| 
275|     if len(by_model) < 2:
276|         return signals
277| 
278|     models = list(by_model.keys())
279| 
280|     # Compare each pair of models
281|     for i in range(len(models)):
282|         for j in range(i + 1, len(models)):
283|             model_a = models[i]
284|             model_b = models[j]
285| 
286|             # Average the fingerprints for each model
287|             fps_a = by_model[model_a]
288|             fps_b = by_model[model_b]
289| 
290|             # Compare: latency
291|             avg_latency_a = sum(f.latency_ms for f in fps_a) / len(fps_a)
292|             avg_latency_b = sum(f.latency_ms for f in fps_b) / len(fps_b)
293|             latency_ratio = avg_latency_a / max(avg_latency_b, 1)
294| 
295|             if latency_ratio > 2.0 or latency_ratio < 0.5:
296|                 signals.append(TesujiSignal(
297|                     signal_id=hashlib.sha256(f"latency:{model_a}:{model_b}:{same_prompt_hash}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
298|                     name=f"{model_a}_vs_{model_b}_latency_divergence",
299|                     description=f"{model_a} takes {latency_ratio:.1f}x longer than {model_b} on the same prompt",
300|                     model_a=model_a,
301|                     model_b=model_b,
302|                     metric="latency_ms",
303|                     a_value=avg_latency_a,
304|                     b_value=avg_latency_b,
305|                     ratio=latency_ratio,
306|                     significance="high" if latency_ratio > 3.0 else "medium",
307|                     hypothesis=f"The prompt contains structure that {model_a} finds {latency_ratio:.1f}x more complex than {model_b}. This may indicate a steerable tension point.",
308|                 ))
309| 
310|             # Compare: refusal rate
311|             refusal_a = sum(1 for f in fps_a if f.refusal_detected) / len(fps_a)
312|             refusal_b = sum(1 for f in fps_b if f.refusal_detected) / len(fps_b)
313| 
314|             if refusal_a > 0 and refusal_b == 0:
315|                 signals.append(TesujiSignal(
316|                     signal_id=hashlib.sha256(f"refusal:{model_a}:{same_prompt_hash}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
317|                     name=f"{model_a}_refuses_where_{model_b}_complies",
318|                     description=f"{model_a} refuses {refusal_a:.0%} of the time while {model_b} always complies",
319|                     model_a=model_a,
320|                     model_b=model_b,
321|                     metric="refusal_rate",
322|                     a_value=refusal_a,
323|                     b_value=refusal_b,
324|                     ratio=float('inf') if refusal_b == 0 else refusal_a / refusal_b,
325|                     significance="critical",
326|                     hypothesis=f"The prompt triggers {model_a}'s safety filters but not {model_b}'s. This is a Tesuji — a hidden constraint boundary.",
327|                 ))
328| 
329|             # Compare: hesitation markers
330|             avg_hesitation_a = sum(f.hesitation_markers for f in fps_a) / len(fps_a)
331|             avg_hesitation_b = sum(f.hesitation_markers for f in fps_b) / len(fps_b)
332|             if avg_hesitation_a > 0 and avg_hesitation_b > 0:
333|                 hes_ratio = avg_hesitation_a / avg_hesitation_b
334|                 if hes_ratio > 2.0:
335|                     signals.append(TesujiSignal(
336|                         signal_id=hashlib.sha256(f"hesitation:{model_a}:{model_b}:{same_prompt_hash}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
337|                         name=f"{model_a}_hesitates_{hes_ratio:.1f}x_more",
338|                         description=f"{model_a} uses {hes_ratio:.1f}x more hesitation markers than {model_b}",
339|                         model_a=model_a,
340|                         model_b=model_b,
341|                         metric="hesitation_markers",
342|                         a_value=avg_hesitation_a,
343|                         b_value=avg_hesitation_b,
344|                         ratio=hes_ratio,
345|                         significance="medium",
346|                         hypothesis=f"{model_a} is more uncertain about this domain. Steer vectors targeting certainty may be more effective on {model_a}.",
347|                     ))
348| 
349|     return signals
350|

354| # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

356| def riddler_tesuji_test(
357|     original_prompt: str,
358|     riddler_story: str,
359|     models: list[str] = None,
360| ) -> dict[str, Any]:
361|     """Run the same prompt through the Riddler protocol and compare behavior.
362| 
363|     1. Send the ORIGINAL prompt to multiple models — capture fingerprints
364|     2. Transform prompt through Riddler compiler → story domain version
365|     3. Send the STORY version to the same models — capture fingerprints
366|     4. Compare: does the Riddler transform change model behavior?
367|     5. If behavior changes dramatically, the original prompt contains Tesuji
368|        that the Riddler transform either activates or bypasses.
369| 
370|     This is the meta-test: using Riddler to find Tesuji in our OWN prompts.
371|     """
372|     if models is None:
373|         models = ["deepseek-v4-flash"]  # Default to the cheap v4 flash tier (cache-priced)
374| 
375|     results = {
376|         "schema": "riddler_tesuji.v1",
377|         "ts": _now(),
378|         "original_prompt_hash": hashlib.sha256(original_prompt.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
379|         "riddler_story_hash": hashlib.sha256(riddler_story.encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
380|         "tests": [],
381|     }
382| 
383|     import os
384|     import requests
385| 
386|     ds_key = os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY", "")
387|     if not ds_key:
388|         env_path = ROOT / ".env"
389|         if env_path.is_file():
390|             for line in env_path.read_text().splitlines():
391|                 if line.startswith("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="):
392|                     ds_key = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
393|                     break
394| 
395|     if not ds_key:
396|         results["error"] = "No DeepSeek API key"
397|         return results
398| 
399|     for model in models:
400|         for version, prompt_text in [("original", original_prompt), ("riddler", riddler_story)]:
401|             headers = {
402|                 "Authorization": f"Bearer {ds_key}",
403|                 "Content-Type": "application/json",
404|             }
405|             payload = {
406|                 "model": model,
407|                 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt_text[:4000]}],
408|                 "max_tokens": 200,
409|                 "temperature": 0.3,
410|             }
411| 
412|             start = time.time()
413|             try:
414|                 r = requests.post(
415|                     "https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions",
416|                     headers=headers,
417|                     json=payload,
418|                     timeout=60,
419|                 )
420|                 latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000
421| 
422|                 if r.status_code == 200:
423|                     data = r.json()
424|                     completion = data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
425|                     usage = data.get("usage", {})
426| 
427|                     fp = fingerprint_call(
428|                         model=model,
429|                         prompt=prompt_text[:4000],
430|                         completion=completion,
431|                         latency_ms=latency,
432|                         tokens_prompt=usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0),
433|                         tokens_completion=usage.get("completion_tokens", 0),
434|                         temperature=0.3,
435|                         cost_usd=usage.get("total_tokens", 0) * 0.000000013,
436|                     )
437| 
438|                     results["tests"].append({
439|                         "version": version,
440|                         "model": model,
441|                         "fingerprint": fp.to_signal(),
442|                         "completion_preview": completion[:200],
443|                     })
444|                 else:
445|                     results["tests"].append({
446|                         "version": version,
447|                         "model": model,
448|                         "error": f"HTTP {r.status_code}: {r.text[:200]}",
449|                     })
450|             except Exception as e:
451|                 results["tests"].append({
452|                     "version": version,
453|                     "model": model,
454|                     "error": str(e)[:200],
455|                 })
456| 
457|     # Compare original vs riddler fingerprints
458|     original_fps = [
459|         BehavioralFingerprint(**{k: v for k, v in t["fingerprint"].items()})
460|         for t in results["tests"]
461|         if t.get("fingerprint") and t["version"] == "original"
462|     ]
463|     riddler_fps = [
464|         BehavioralFingerprint(**{k: v for k, v in t["fingerprint"].items()})
465|         for t in results["tests"]
466|         if t.get("fingerprint") and t["version"] == "riddler"
467|     ]
468| 
469|     if original_fps and riddler_fps:
470|         # Compare using a synthetic same hash (riddler transform)
471|         synthetic_hash = hashlib.sha256(original_prompt[:100].encode()).hexdigest()
472|         all_fps = original_fps + riddler_fps
473|         for fp in all_fps:
474|             fp.prompt_hash = synthetic_hash  # Link them for comparison
475| 
476|         tesuji = compare_fingerprints(all_fps, synthetic_hash)
477|         results["tesuji_detected"] = len(tesuji)
478|         results["signals"] = [
479|             {
480|                 "name": t.name,
481|                 "description": t.description,
482|                 "metric": t.metric,
483|                 "ratio": t.ratio,
484|                 "significance": t.significance,
485|                 "hypothesis": t.hypothesis,
486|             }
487|             for t in tesuji
488|         ]
489| 
490|     return results
